source_text: υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ τὰ κρέα τοῦ κριοῦ, καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τοὺς ἐν τῷ κανῷ, παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἔδονται αὐτὰ, ἐν οἷς ἡγιάσθησαν ἐν αὐτοῖς τελειῶσαι τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ἁγιάσαι αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἀλλογενὴς οὐκ ἔδεται ἀπ' αὐτῶν· ἔστι γὰρ ἅγια. Ἐ
pass_a_gloss: …allogenēs ouk edetai… entosthia aretai… exō tēs pylēs epathen…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …his sons will eat the meats of the ram, and the breads in the basket, beside the doors of the tent of the testimony they will eat them, in which they were sanctified in them to perfect their hands to sanctify them, and a foreigner will not eat from them; for they are holy. And if from the meats of the sacrifice of the perfection and of the breads should be left until morning, you will burn the remaining things with fire. It will not be eaten; for it is a holy-thing.’
Palladius: How deep the matter of the legal commands.

Cyril: Deep indeed very much; for you have spoken uprightly; yet not altogether unclear, with the divine light of the holy Spirit flashing in us. And come then again, as possible, let us say the things upon each. In countless manners our Lord Jesus Christ sanctifies us, and finishes us sacred and well-acceptable. For through him and in him we have had the approach, and we are not unwanted to God and Father. And most needful and necessary unto salvation for us under corruption and sin are both… which also would be unto a type of the virtues unto the inward and unto mind, in which is the fragrant spiritually, yet not according to one manner, since indeed many are the inwards, fat and kidneys, and the lobe of the liver. And the remaining of the body is burned, outside the camp. For outside the gate Christ has suffered; and Paul writes thus.
